analysis: The PR is documentation-only: docs/reference/configuration.md gains two table rows (head lines 401-402) for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY. Both are performance toggles for the Qwen inline-MTP path, default on, disabled by 0/false/no/off, read in libs/mlx-swift-lm/.../MTPContractsV2.swift, and documented as not forwarded to LaunchAgents. The change adds no code and does not touch the coordinator WebSocket contract (TB-002), attestation or App Attest authorization (TB-009, TB-011), keys (A-002, A-003), the prefix cache (T-041) or the fan helper. The new rows state that the toggles only choose between scheduling and seeding modes, which does not alter the E2E encryption, the KV cache scoping or the account salt. Nothing in the rows broadens the attack surface or contradicts the threat model. The documented behavior itself (ordinary chainable decode, carry seeded from the final prompt row hidden) is outside the supplied evidence, because the Swift implementation in MTPContractsV2.swift was not provided. I therefore cannot confirm the docs match the code or that the new carry/history paths preserve per-request isolation. That is a documentation-accuracy question, not a demonstrated security regression. The unchanged base text (docs/reference/configuration.md lines 354-519) was read for context; it has no pre-existing issue that this PR affects.
